annotation.title_en: Regulations on the Management of Remotely Piloted Aircraft (Drones)
annotation.authors_or_issuer: 交通部 (Ministry of Transportation and Communications, Taiwan)
annotation.venue: 全國法規資料庫 / Ministry of Transportation and Communications
annotation.summary_en: Taiwan's binding Ministry of Transportation rules under the Civil Aviation Act governing remotely piloted aircraft. They cover registration, RF identification and geofencing, type and physical inspection, manufacturer and importer product registration, operator licensing, operating limits, permits for institutional operators, and incident reporting.
key_provisions_or_claims: Drones of 250 g or more and all institution-owned drones must be registered with the CAA; registration is valid for two years.
Drones of 1 kg or more with navigation equipment must have geofencing software to keep out of no-fly and restricted zones.
Design, manufacture and import require type inspection or approval; drones of 25 kg or more also need physical inspection.
Operator certificates (learner, general, professional) are required for heavier or institutional drones, with age and testing requirements.
Safety incidents must be reported within 24 hours; operating limits include 30 m clearance and a maximum extended visual line of sight range of 900 m.
